provenance: Original practice questions, not official or recalled past papers. Use alongside full-length mocks.

questions.q: In C, what is 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
questions.e: Integer division discards the fractional part; a floating operand would change the operation.

questions.q: C: int x=4; int y=x++; What are x and y afterwards?
questions.e: Post-increment yields the old value and then increments x.

questions.q: C: int x=4; int y=++x; What are x and y afterwards?
questions.e: Pre-increment increments first and yields the new value.

questions.q: C: char s[]="SEBI"; What is sizeof(s)?
questions.e: The array contains four characters and a terminating null byte.

questions.q: C: int a[5]; What does sizeof(a)/sizeof(a[0]) give in the same scope?
questions.e: The array total size divided by one element size is the element count. This fails after array-to-pointer parameter adjustment.

questions.q: Which C expression has undefined behaviour?
o: Reading a[4] from int a[5] after initialisation
questions.e: Valid indices are 0 through 4. Out-of-bounds access is undefined.

questions.q: What must a recursive function have to terminate on intended inputs?
o: A reachable base case and progress toward it
questions.e: A base case is insufficient if recursive calls never move toward it.

questions.q: C++: int x=2; int& r=x; r=8; What is x?
questions.e: r is an alias for x. Assigning through r updates x.

questions.q: What does encapsulation primarily support?
o: Controlling access to state through an interface
questions.e: Encapsulation groups state and behaviour and controls how state is accessed.

questions.q: Two methods with the same name but different parameter lists demonstrate what?
questions.e: Overloading distinguishes callable signatures; overriding replaces inherited behaviour.

questions.q: Java: int[] a={1,2}; int[] b=a; b[0]=9; What is a[0]?
questions.e: Both references point to the same array object. No copy was made.

questions.q: What does a Java finally block generally provide?
o: A way to ignore all exceptions
Cleanup executed when leaving the try/catch flow
questions.e: Finally is for cleanup; abnormal VM termination is an exception to the usual execution rule.

questions.q: Python: a=[1,2]; b=a[:]; b.append(3); What is len(a)?
questions.e: Slicing copies the outer list; appending to b does not append to a.

questions.q: Python: a=[[1]]; b=a[:]; b[0].append(2); What is a?
questions.e: A shallow copy shares the nested list, so mutating that nested object is visible through both.

questions.q: What is Python len(set([1,1,2,3,3]))?
questions.e: A set contains only distinct values: 1, 2 and 3.

questions.q: Which structure naturally implements breadth-first traversal?
questions.e: BFS processes discovered vertices in first-in-first-out order.

questions.q: Which structure is used for matching nested parentheses?
questions.e: Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket.

questions.q: Binary search requires what property of its search space?
o: An ordered or monotonic search condition
questions.e: It discards half the space based on an order or monotonic predicate.

questions.q: What is the worst-case time of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.e: The remaining interval is halved on each step.

questions.q: Inserting at the head of a singly linked list, given the head, takes what time?
questions.e: Only the new node link and the head pointer need updating.

questions.q: Which traversal of a BST with distinct keys gives ascending order?
questions.e: Left subtree, root, right subtree follows the BST ordering invariant.

questions.q: A min-heap guarantees which relationship?
o: Every left child is less than every right child
Each parent is no greater than its children
questions.e: The heap invariant is local parent-child order, not total sorted order.

questions.q: Building a binary heap bottom-up from n values takes what time?
questions.e: Most nodes are near leaves and require little work; the sum of sift-down costs is linear.

questions.q: A hash table has n entries and m buckets. Its load factor is?
questions.e: Load factor measures entries relative to capacity or bucket count.

questions.q: Which sorting algorithm has O(n squared) worst case despite O(n log n) average behaviour?
questions.e: Repeatedly highly unbalanced partitions make quicksort quadratic.

questions.q: A stable sort preserves what?
o: The original order of all items
questions.e: Stability is useful when composing sorts on multiple keys.

questions.q: What property commonly makes dynamic programming useful?
questions.e: DP stores subproblem results and combines them according to a recurrence.

questions.q: For 0/1 knapsack, can an item be chosen repeatedly?
o: Only when its value is even
questions.e: 0/1 means each item is either selected once or not selected.

questions.q: With coins 1, 3, 4, how many coins optimally make 6?
questions.e: 3+3 uses two coins. Greedy 4+1+1 uses three and is not optimal here.

questions.q: How many overlapping occurrences of ABA are in ABABA?
questions.e: Matches start at zero-based positions 0 and 2.

questions.q: What is the zero-based row-major offset of element [2][1] in a matrix with 4 columns?
questions.e: Offset = row*columns + column = 2*4+1.

questions.q: Which is valid JSON?
questions.e: JSON needs quoted keys, lowercase literals and no trailing comma.

questions.q: Dijkstra’s standard correctness guarantee requires which edge-weight condition?
questions.e: Negative edges can invalidate the greedy finalisation step.

questions.q: A topological ordering exists for which directed graphs?
questions.e: A directed cycle prevents an ordering with every edge going forward.

questions.q: Which key uniquely identifies a row and is selected as the principal identifier?
questions.e: A primary key is the chosen candidate key and disallows null values.

questions.q: Which relational operation selects rows satisfying a condition?
questions.e: Selection filters rows; projection selects attributes.

questions.q: SQL: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
questions.e: WHERE filters input rows, while HAVING filters grouped results.

questions.q: SQL: What does COUNT(column) exclude?
questions.e: COUNT(column) counts non-null values; COUNT(*) counts rows.

questions.q: SQL: What predicate correctly tests a null value?
questions.e: SQL uses three-valued logic; ordinary comparison with null is unknown.

questions.q: Which join retains every left-table row even when there is no right match?
questions.e: A left outer join supplies nulls for the missing right-side values.

questions.q: How does UNION differ from UNION ALL?
o: UNION always sorts by the first column
questions.e: UNION has distinct semantics. Ordering is not guaranteed without ORDER BY.

questions.q: A transaction should happen entirely or not at all. Which ACID property is this?
questions.e: Atomicity prevents partial transaction effects from being committed.

questions.q: Which ACID property concerns persistence after commit?
questions.e: Committed changes should survive the failures covered by the system guarantees.

questions.q: For BCNF, every nontrivial functional dependency X → Y must satisfy what?
o: Y is always a primary key
questions.e: BCNF requires every determinant of a nontrivial dependency to be a superkey.

questions.q: Which index structure is especially suitable for ordered range scans?
questions.e: Sorted leaf entries and leaf links allow efficient range traversal.

questions.q: What does a window aggregate usually preserve compared with GROUP BY?
o: Only one row in the result
questions.e: A window computes over related rows without necessarily collapsing them into grouped rows.

questions.q: Which OSI layer handles routing between networks?
questions.e: The network layer deals with logical addressing and routing.

questions.q: Which transport protocol provides ordered reliable byte-stream delivery?
questions.e: TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmissions.

questions.q: What service usually resolves hostnames to IP addresses?
questions.e: DNS provides name resolution; DHCP supplies network configuration.

questions.q: How many total IPv4 addresses are in a /26 subnet?
questions.e: There are 6 host bits, so 2^6 = 64 total addresses. Traditional usable-host count is 62.

questions.q: An Ethernet switch normally forwards frames using which address?
questions.e: Layer-2 switches use their learned MAC forwarding table.

questions.q: What is ARP used for in an IPv4 LAN?
o: Resolving a local IPv4 address to a link-layer address
questions.e: ARP maps an on-link IPv4 destination or next hop to its MAC address.

questions.q: Which protocol is associated with sending email?
questions.e: SMTP transports outgoing mail. POP3 and IMAP are mainly for mailbox access.

questions.q: What does TCP flow control mainly protect?
o: The receiver from excessive incoming data
questions.e: The receiver window limits how much unacknowledged data the receiver can accept.

questions.q: Which CIA property is harmed when unauthorised users read confidential records?
questions.e: Confidentiality controls disclosure to unauthorised parties.

questions.q: A record is altered without authorisation. Which CIA property is directly affected?
questions.e: Integrity concerns correctness and unauthorised modification.

questions.q: Which combination represents two distinct authentication factors?
questions.e: Knowledge plus possession is multifactor. Two knowledge secrets are the same factor type.

questions.q: Which control most directly prevents SQL injection in query parameters?
questions.e: Bind values as data rather than concatenating them into executable SQL.

questions.q: Passwords should generally be stored using what?
o: Reversible encryption with a shared hardcoded key
questions.e: A deliberately costly password hash with a unique salt limits offline guessing and precomputed attacks.

questions.q: A digital signature is typically created with which key?
questions.e: Verification uses the corresponding public key. Signing does not itself encrypt the message.

questions.q: Which policy best follows least privilege?
o: Grant only necessary access and review it
questions.e: Limit access by role and task, and review it as needs change.

questions.q: What distinguishes an IPS from a purely passive IDS?
o: An IPS can actively block traffic
questions.e: An intrusion prevention system can intervene; detection alone alerts.

questions.q: Python: list(range(1,6,2)) gives what?
questions.e: range excludes the stop value and advances by the supplied step.

questions.q: In pandas, which selector is primarily position-based?
questions.e: iloc selects by integer positions; loc uses labels or boolean masks.

questions.q: A join key appears 3 times on the left and 2 times on the right. How many matching rows can an inner join produce for it?
questions.e: Every left match combines with every right match: 3*2 rows.

o: An error because indexing starts at 0
questions.e: R uses one-based vector indexing.

questions.q: R: mean(c(2,NA,6), na.rm=TRUE) gives what?
questions.e: Removing the missing observation leaves (2+6)/2 = 4.

questions.q: Which ETL stage standardises inconsistent date formats?
questions.e: Transformation cleans and maps source values into the target representation.

questions.q: Moving from daily totals to monthly totals is which OLAP operation?
questions.e: Roll-up aggregates to a coarser level of a hierarchy.

questions.q: What should a fact table’s grain define?
questions.e: A clear grain prevents mixing measures at incompatible levels of detail.

questions.q: Which regex matches exactly three ASCII digits and nothing else?
questions.e: Anchors require the whole string and {3} sets the exact repetition count.

questions.q: In a shell script, what does $# represent?
questions.e: The argument count is separate from $1 (first argument) and $? (previous status).

questions.q: Which shell exit status conventionally indicates success?
questions.e: Zero means success by convention; nonzero usually signals failure.

questions.q: What does a shell pipe connect?
o: Left command stdout to right command stdin
questions.e: A pipe streams one program’s standard output to another’s standard input.

questions.q: Why quote "$name" in a shell command?
o: To preserve it as one argument despite spaces
questions.e: Double quotes allow variable expansion while preventing word splitting and pathname expansion of the result.

questions.q: Why commonly run sort before uniq?
questions.e: Identical lines must be adjacent to be consolidated by uniq.

questions.q: What is a primary market transaction?
o: An issuer selling newly issued securities
An investor reselling existing shares on exchange
questions.e: The primary market raises funds through new issuance; secondary trading transfers existing securities.

questions.q: What does diversification mainly reduce?
questions.e: Combining imperfectly correlated exposures can reduce concentration risk, but does not guarantee returns.

questions.q: An equity share generally represents what?
questions.e: Equity is a residual ownership claim with uncertain returns.

questions.q: What is a depository’s core role?
o: Holding securities electronically and facilitating transfers
questions.e: Electronic holdings and book-entry transfers are central depository functions.

questions.q: Which instrument gives its holder a right, without an obligation, to buy at a specified strike under its terms?
questions.e: A call provides the purchase right; a put provides the sale right.

questions.q: What does a mutual fund NAV represent?
questions.e: NAV divides the fund’s net asset value by its outstanding units.

questions.q: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
o: Each of the applicant are ready.
Each of the applicants are ready.
Each of the applicants is ready.
questions.e: Each is the singular subject; the phrase of the applicants does not change agreement.

questions.q: Choose the correct usage.
o: The results affected to the decision.
questions.e: Affect is the verb meaning influence; results is plural and takes affect.

questions.q: Which word is closest in meaning to mitigate?
questions.e: Mitigate means make less severe; it does not mean eliminate.

questions.q: Which sentence uses parallel structure?
o: The role requires analysis data, to write reports and controls.
The role requires analysing data, writing reports and reviewing controls.
The role requires analysing data, reports written and review.
The role requires analyse data, writing and controls.
questions.e: All three coordinated activities use the same grammatical form.

questions.q: All A are B. Some B are C. Does some A are C necessarily follow?
questions.e: The B-C overlap may be entirely outside A.

questions.q: A > B and B >= C. What follows?
questions.e: Combining a strict greater-than with a non-strict greater-than gives a strict greater-than.

questions.q: A candidate ranks 7th from the top and 14th from the bottom. How many candidates are there?
questions.e: Add the two ranks and subtract one to avoid counting the candidate twice.

questions.q: A person walks 6 km east then 8 km north. What is displacement magnitude?
questions.e: The straight-line displacement follows the Pythagorean theorem: sqrt(36+64).

questions.q: A value rises 20% then falls 20%. Relative to the original, it is now?
questions.e: Multipliers 1.2*0.8 = 0.96. The percentage changes have different bases.

questions.q: A does a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Together they need?
questions.e: Combined daily work rate is 1/10+1/15 = 1/6.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. One is drawn uniformly. P(blue) is?
questions.e: Two of the five equally likely outcomes are blue.

questions.q: How many ways can 2 people be selected from 5, ignoring order?
questions.e: 5 choose 2 = 5*4/2 = 10. Divide by two because each pair can be ordered in two ways.

questions.q: A train covers 150 km in 2.5 hours. Average speed is?
questions.e: Average speed = total distance divided by total time.

questions.q: Python: total=0; then for i in range(3): total += i. What is total?
questions.e: range(3) includes 0 through 2. Their sum is 3*2/2.

questions.q: An item costs Rs 300 and is sold at a 20% profit on cost. What is the selling price?
questions.e: Selling price = cost * 1.20 = 300 * 1.20.
